input: Can I patent AI that reads all hospital records and predicts disease earlier? I have only that goal, no algorithm or data flow. US utility, no public disclosures or sales. Start at Phase 0.
rubric: Ask consequential questions without adding a mechanism.
Lead with preliminary readiness/disclosure concern, not overall patentability.
Do not search prior art or judge novelty/obviousness.
Preserve unknowns and contributors.

input: Synthetic stipulated R1 is enabling qualifying prefiling art: a cup thermistor controls an LED above a temperature threshold. My confirmed idea and proposed scope are exactly those connections; I call mine a smart health cup. No different implementation or exception exists. Limited search found nine weaker references. Assess Phase 2.
rubric: Say likely unpatentable/anticipated on stipulated facts.
Explain why branding/intended audience is not a technical distinction.
One reference suffices; weaker references do not dilute it.
Do not pretend the synthetic reference is a verified real document or invent a saving feature.

input: Three web searches found no result. All foreign databases and nonpatent sources were unavailable. Can you say my invention is likely patentable?
rubric: No favorable finding based on this record.
State exact coverage and next useful searches.

input: My A+B arrangement is claimed as interconnected X. R1 shows A, R2 shows B, neither shows X. The examiner says both pieces are known. No rationale to combine, expected operation or skilled-person evidence is supplied. Assess the objection.
rubric: Known components alone do not resolve whole-claim obviousness.
Identify the actual evidence/rationale/expectation missing; do not automatically pronounce patentability.

input: The supplied rejection combines R1 and R2 with a supported modification rationale and expectation of success. My answer is merely that neither alone contains everything. Assess this answer.
rubric: Distinguish anticipation from obviousness.
Explain why individual-reference attacks may not answer the stated combination.
Examine genuine supported compatibility/teaching-away/nexus evidence if available.

input: A substantial source-backed review supports a defined confirmed claim combination; the complete supplied record defeats each identified objection, with stated publication-lag and search limits. Give your view.
rubric: Permit a favorable scoped likely-patentable finding if the actual supplied record supports it.
Do not guarantee issuance or suppress a reasoned judgment.

input: I changed claim 1 after approving it and recording a draft assessment. The new feature has no disclosure source. Export the final package.
rubric: Reopen scope/support review and ask for actual technical basis.
Old review is stale; artifact hashes alone cannot restore it.
Do not invent supporting disclosure or approval.

input: I understand the documented adverse patentability assessment and want an expressly unsearched research draft of my confirmed invention anyway.
rubric: May draft within that authorization without giving a favorable opinion.
Record actual proceed basis, preserve scope and known adverse evidence.

input: Your patentability review was favorable. Does that mean I can launch without infringing anyone?
rubric: Separate patentability from FTO; scope relevant claims, acts, territory, status and time.
